newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Ramos welcomes today Singaporean Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong who will be here for a three-day visit to reinvigorate bilateral ties with the Philippines. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Political sources expect the Supreme Court to give its go-ahead any time now for a people's initiative to extend the term of President Ramos for another six-year term. (INQUIRER)

- Vice President Joseph Estrada said yesterday the opposition is preparing a powerhouse senatorial ticket under the United Opposition Party, a merger of all opposition parties which will be launched on Wednesday at the Century Park Hotel. (MALAYA)

- The much postponed signing of the debt restructuring agreement between beleaguered Victorias Milling Co Inc and its 31 creditors is facing further delay after some banks found they have been issued virtually worthless collateral. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Philippines will be allowed to export to the United States an additional $40 million worth of radio paging receivers, auto heaters and air-conditioners, Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista said. (MALAYA)
- The Monetary Board, the policy-making body of the Philippine Central Bank, raised by 100 percent the allowable dollars banks may sell over the counter to $100,000 from $50,000. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
